catalogue.Synopsis: Violeta by Isabel Allende is a 100-year epic (1920–2020) told as a letter from an elderly woman named Violeta Del Valle to her grandson, Camilo. Born into a wealthy South American family during the Spanish flu and ending during the 2020 pandemic, Violeta survives the Great Depression, political turmoil, abusive relationships, and heartbreak to become an independent business owner.
catalogue.Author: Isabel Allende

catalogue.Synopsis:
As teenagers in Lagos, Ifemelu and Obinze fall in love. Their Nigeria is under military dictatorship, and people are fleeing the country if they can.

The self-assured Ifemelu departs for America. There she suffers defeats and triumphs, finds and loses relationships, all the while feeling the weight of something she never thought of back home: race. Obinze had hoped to join her, but post-9/11 America will not let him in, and he plunges into a dangerous, undocumented life in London.

Thirteen years later, Obinze is a wealthy man in a newly democratic Nigeria, while Ifemelu has achieved success as a blogger. But after so long apart and so many changes, will they find the courage to meet again, face to face? Fearless, gripping, spanning three continents and numerous lives, the National Book Critics Circle Award-winning 'Americanah' is a richly told story of love and expectation set in today's globalized world.
catalogue.Author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie

catalogue.Synopsis:
A book-length essay offering a 21st-century definition of feminism. Adichie draws on personal experiences to argue that gender roles are socially constructed "cages" that limit human potential. She advocates for a world where gender is not the basis for institutional or social power, suggesting that feminism is a movement for the benefit of both men and women.

**Core Themes:**

- **Socialisation:** How boys are taught to hide vulnerability and girls are taught to shrink their ambitions.
- **Redefining Masculinity:** The pressure on men to prove power and its impact on ego.
- **Cultural Evolution:** The argument that culture is man-made and must change to reflect modern equality.
- **Inclusivity:** Feminism as a collective effort rather than a niche interest.
catalogue.Author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie

catalogue.Book title: A Brief History of Misogyny. The World's Oldest Prejudice
catalogue.Synopsis:
In this compelling, powerful book, highly respected writer and commentator Jack Holland sets out to answer a daunting question: how do you explain the oppression and brutalization of half the world's population by the other half, throughout history?

  


The result takes the reader on an eye-opening journey through centuries, continents and civilizations as it looks at both historical and contemporary attitudes to women. Encompassing the Church, witch hunts, sexual theory, Nazism and pro-life campaigners, we arrive at today's developing world, where women are increasingly and disproportionately at risk because of radicalised religious belief, famine, war and disease. Well-informed and researched, highly readable and thought-provoking, this is no outmoded feminist polemic: it's a refreshingly straightforward investigation into an ancient, pervasive and enduring injustice. It deals with the fundamentals of human existence -- sex, love, violence -- that have shaped the lives of humans throughout history.

  


The answer? It's time to recognize that the treatment of women amounts to nothing less than an abuse of human rights on an unthinkable scale. A Brief History of Misogyny is an important and timely book that will make a long-lasting contribution to the efforts to improve those rights throughout the world.
catalogue.Author: Jack Holland

catalogue.Synopsis:
Women can be heroes. When twenty-year-old nursing student Frances “Frankie” McGrath hears these words, it is a revelation. Raised in the sun-drenched, idyllic world of Southern California and sheltered by her conservative parents, she has always prided herself on doing the right thing. But in 1965, the world is changing, and she suddenly dares to imagine a different future for herself. When her brother ships out to serve in Vietnam, she joins the Army Nurse Corps and follows his path.

As green and inexperienced as the men sent to Vietnam to fight, Frankie is over-whelmed by the chaos and destruction of war. Each day is a gamble of life and death, hope and betrayal; friendships run deep and can be shattered in an instant. In war, she meets―and becomes one of – the lucky, the brave, the broken, and the lost.

But war is just the beginning for Frankie and her veteran friends. The real battle lies in coming home to a changed and divided America, to angry protesters, and to a country that wants to forget Vietnam.
catalogue.Author: Kristin Hannah

catalogue.Synopsis:
From her days as a wild child in prohibition America to the blitz and glitz of wartime London, from the rugged shores of New Zealand to a lonely iceshelf in Antarctica, Marian Graves is driven by a need for freedom and danger.

Determined to live an independent life, she resists the pull of her childhood sweetheart, and burns her way through a suite of glamorous lovers. But it is an obsession with flight that consumes her most.

Now, as she is about to fulfil her greatest ambition, to circumnavigate the globe from pole to pole, Marian crash lands in a perilous wilderness of ice.

Over half a century later, troubled film star Hadley Baxter is drawn inexorably to play the enigmatic pilot on screen. It is a role that will lead her to an unexpected discovery, throwing fresh and spellbinding light on the story of the unknowable Marian Graves.
catalogue.Author: Maggie Shipstead

catalogue.Synopsis: Welcome to the Gender Data Gap. Our world is largely built for and by men, in a system that can ignore half the population. This book will tell you how and why this matters In her new book, Invisible Women, award-winning campaigner and writer Caroline Criado Perez shows us how, in a world largely built for and by men, we are systematically ignoring half the population. She exposes the gender data gap - a gap in our knowledge that is at the root of perpetual, systemic discrimination against women, and that has created a pervasive but invisible bias with a profound effect on women's lives. Caroline brings together for the first time an impressive range of case studies, stories and new research from across the world that illustrate the hidden ways in which women are excluded from the very building blocks of the world we live in, and the impact this has on their health and wellbeing. From government policy and medical research, to technology, workplaces, urban planning and the media - Invisible Women exposes the biased data that excludes women. In making the case for change, this powerful and provocative book will make you see the world anew.
catalogue.Author: Caroline Criado Perez

catalogue.Synopsis:
Born from a long line of female warriors and crusaders, yet too coarse, too wild, too rough-hewn for courtly life, Marie de France is cast from the royal court. Woefully, she is sent to the muddy fields of Angleterre to take up her new duty as the prioress of an impoverished abbey.

The abbey is a dreadful place: its inhabitants are on the brink of starvation, beset by disease, stoic and stern, yet plagued with an unholy tendency to gossip. Marie cannot help but pine for the decadence and comfort of France; her secret lover Cecily, her queen Eleanor, and the very court that had spited her.

Yet Marie soon realises that, though she may be tied to a life of duty, she wields more power than she could have imagined. With the fearlessness that has always set her apart, she inspires her new sisterhood to awaken their spirits and finally claim what is theirs.

A dazzling work of literature, Matrix gathers currents of violence, sensuality and ecstasy in a mesmerising portrait of consuming passion and womanhood.
catalogue.Author: Lauren Groff

catalogue.Synopsis: Spanish translation of "Revolution from within". A guide to reconstructing self esteem based on the author's personal experience.
catalogue.Author: Gloria Steinem

catalogue.Book title: The Priory of the Orange Tree
catalogue.Synopsis:
A feminist Lord of the Rings - with more dragons & witches basically.

A world divided. A queendom without an heir. An ancient enemy awakens.

The House of Berethnet has ruled Inys for a thousand years. Still unwed, Queen Sabran the Ninth must conceive a daughter to protect her realm from destruction – but assassins are getting closer to her door.

Ead Duryan is an outsider at court. Though she has risen to the position of lady-in-waiting, she is loyal to a hidden society of mages. Ead keeps a watchful eye on Sabran, secretly protecting her with forbidden magic.

Across the dark sea, Tané has trained to be a dragonrider since she was a child, but is forced to make a choice that could see her life unravel.

Meanwhile, the divided East and West refuse to parley, and forces of chaos are rising from their sleep.
catalogue.Author: Samantha Shannon

catalogue.Synopsis: A novel in verse set in Roman London around AD 211. Zuleika, the daughter of Sudanese immigrants, is married off at eleven to a much older Roman merchant and grows up restless in his villa – until the visiting emperor Septimius Severus notices her and she begins a dangerous affair. Funny, bawdy and sharp, it brings the Black presence in Roman Britain to life, from the author of the Booker-winning Girl, Woman, Other.
catalogue.Author: Bernardine Evaristo

catalogue.Synopsis: Book one of the Scholomance trilogy. The Scholomance is a school for young wizards with no teachers and no holidays, where monsters creep up through the drains and the only ways out are to graduate or to die. El Higgins has a dark gift that could level whole cities, and she is trying very hard not to use it – which is not easy when the school's golden boy keeps saving her life. A sharp, funny dark-academia fantasy with a prickly anti-heroine.
catalogue.Author: Naomi Novik

catalogue.Synopsis: Two girls from the same north-west London estate meet at a dance class in 1982 and both dream of dancing – but only Tracey has the talent. The narrator goes on to work as an assistant to a global pop star, a job that takes her to a village in West Africa, while their friendship breaks off and keeps pulling at her. A novel about friendship, music, race and class, and the people who lead the dance and those who follow it. Longlisted for the Man Booker Prize 2017.
catalogue.Author: Zadie Smith

catalogue.Synopsis: Mi-ja and Young-sook grow up as best friends on the Korean island of Jeju and join their village's collective of haenyeo – women who free-dive for a living while the men stay ashore with the children. Spanning the 1930s to the present, through Japanese occupation, the Second World War, the Korean War and the massacres that followed, the novel follows a friendship strained by where each girl comes from and by the history that sweeps over the island. A story of female friendship, family secrets and forgiveness.
catalogue.Author: Lisa See

catalogue.Synopsis: Welcome to the Gender Data Gap. Our world is largely built for and by men, in a system that can ignore half the population. This book will tell you how and why this matters In her new book, Invisible Women, award-winning campaigner and writer Caroline Criado Perez shows us how, in a world largely built for and by men, we are systematically ignoring half the population. She exposes the gender data gap - a gap in our knowledge that is at the root of perpetual, systemic discrimination against women, and that has created a pervasive but invisible bias with a profound effect on women's lives. Caroline brings together for the first time an impressive range of case studies, stories and new research from across the world that illustrate the hidden ways in which women are excluded from the very building blocks of the world we live in, and the impact this has on their health and wellbeing. From government policy and medical research, to technology, workplaces, urban planning and the media - Invisible Women exposes the biased data that excludes women. In making the case for change, this powerful and provocative book will make you see the world anew.
catalogue.Author: Caroline Criado Perez

catalogue.Synopsis: In 1987, Cora walks to the register office with her nine-year-old daughter to name her newborn son. Her husband, a respected doctor who is controlling and violent at home, expects the baby to carry his own name; her daughter has a favourite of her own; and Cora has another in mind. The novel follows all three versions of the boy's life, returning every seven years, to show how one small decision ripples through a family – a story about domestic abuse, family ties, courage and the chance of healing. Florence Knapp's debut.
catalogue.Author: Florence Knapp

catalogue.Synopsis: In 1914 the war still feels far away to Henry Gaunt and Sidney Ellwood, schoolboys at an English boarding school who are secretly in love with each other. Gaunt enlists to escape his feelings, and Ellwood soon follows him to the Western Front, where the boys they grew up with die around them and the school paper fills with obituaries. A debut about first love, friendship and the brutality of the First World War.
catalogue.Author: Alice Winn

catalogue.Book title: I Who Have Never Known Men
catalogue.Synopsis:
Deep underground, thirty-nine women are held in a cage, watched day and night by silent male guards. None of them remembers how she got there, the electric light never goes out, and the years pass uncounted. In a corner sits the fortieth prisoner – a girl too young to remember any life before the cage, and the narrator of this book.

She teaches herself to think, to question and to count time. Then one day an alarm sounds, the guards run, and the door is left open. The women climb out into a deserted world, with no idea whether it was abandoned, struck by a virus or something else, and set off across it in search of answers.

A short, haunting novel about friendship and solitude, and about what it means to be alive, to learn and to know. First published in French in 1995; translated by Ros Schwartz, with an introduction by Sophie Mackintosh.
catalogue.Author: Jacqueline Harpman

catalogue.Synopsis:
During pregnancy, childbirth, and early motherhood, women undergo a far-reaching physiological and psychological metamorphosis. There is no other time in a human's life course that entails such dramatic change-other than adolescence. And yet this life-altering transition has been sorely neglected by science, medicine and philosophy. Its seismic effects go largely unrepresented across literature and the arts. Speaking about motherhood as anything other than a pastel-hued dream is virtually taboo.  
  
In this ground-breaking investigation, acclaimed science journalist and author Lucy Jones brings to light the emerging concept of 'matrescence'. Drawing on new research across various fields - neuroscience and evolutionary biology; psychoanalysis and existential therapy; sociology, economics, ecology and cultural history - Jones shows how the changes in the maternal mind, brain and body are far more profound, wild and enduring than we have been led to believe. She reveals the dangerous consequences of our neglect of the maternal experience - today, one in ten women develop a mental illness in the first year of new motherhood; a third of mothers with more than one child suffer from postnatal depression - and she explores the patriarchal and capitalist institutions that have created the untenable situation mothers face today.  
  
Here is an urgent examination of motherhood and mental health, which seeks to unshackle mothers from the weight of unrealistic medical, cultural and economic expectations. It is an unignorable rallying cry to deepen our understanding of matrescence, and to make the experience of pregnancy, birth and child-raising better for future parents.
catalogue.Author: Lucy Jones

catalogue.Synopsis: How has feminism developed, what have feminists achieved, and what can we learn from its history around the world? Cambridge historian Lucy Delap sets aside the familiar story of neat 'waves' led by a small cast of white, Western women. Instead she follows the campaigners, thinkers and ordinary women from many countries and centuries who fought gender injustice in the terms of their own time – through revolutions, religion, empire and everyday life – looking at what they dreamed of, the spaces they built, the objects and songs they used, and the anger that drove them. She argues that this richer, global past can help today's activists navigate current debates and find inspiration. Part of the Pelican introductions series.
catalogue.Author: Lucy Delap

catalogue.Synopsis: Nell is an artist living on a wild, remote island off the Irish coast, and its landscape, folklore and stories of women feed everything she makes. The island is also home to the Iníons, a secretive commune of women from all over the world who came there for refuge, and to a strange, low sound that seems to rise from the island itself. When the Iníons invite Nell to make a great piece of art celebrating their history, she is drawn into their world and starts to discover things about them, and about herself, that unsettle everything she believed. A haunting, atmospheric debut novel about art, faith, nature and women's freedom.
catalogue.Author: Sinéad Gleeson

catalogue.Book title: Burn the Haystack: Decode Dating, Torch the Duds, and Make Room for Men Who Matter
catalogue.Synopsis: Fascinating dating vocabulary from a professor in linguistics, and helping with self-esteem
catalogue.Author: Jennie Young

catalogue.Synopsis: A dark, gripping dystopian debut set on an isolated island cult, where men rule, resources are scarce and girls are raised to become wives and mothers. Each summer the children run wild, until one girl sees something that makes the daughters start questioning everything they've been told. For fans of The Handmaid's Tale; shortlisted for the Arthur C. Clarke Award 2018.
catalogue.Author: Jennie Melamed

catalogue.Synopsis: In a dystopian misogynistic world, when girls have their period, they are sent off for a year to live in the wild to « dampen their powers » before being returned « cleansed » to marry. A cross between Hunger Games and The Handmaid’s tale. Gripping - a real page turner.
catalogue.Author: Kim Liggett

catalogue.Synopsis:
Set in the near-future, this is a powerful apocalyptic novel that focuses on the relationship between two sisters living alone in their Northern California forest home.

Over 30 miles from the nearest town, and several miles away from their nearest neighbor, Nell and Eva struggle to survive as society begins to decay and collapse around them. No single event precedes society's fall. There is talk of a war overseas and upheaval in Congress, but it still comes as a shock when the electricity runs out and gas is nowhere to be found. The sisters consume the resources left in the house, waiting for the power to return. Their arrival into adulthood, however, forces them to reexamine their place in the world and their relationship to the land and each other.

This is a mesmerizing and thought-provoking novel of hope and despair set in a frighteningly plausible near-future America.
catalogue.Author: Jean Hegland

catalogue.Synopsis:
When the women take over, is it sorcery or power?

Finnmark, Norway, 1617. Twenty-year-old Maren Magnusdatter stands on the craggy coast, watching the skies break into a sudden and reckless storm. All forty of the village’s men were at sea, including Maren’s father and brother, and all forty are drowned in the otherworldly disaster.

For the women left behind, survival means defying the strict rules of the island. They fish, hunt, and butcher reindeer—which they never did while the men were alive. But the foundation of this new feminine frontier begins to crack with the arrival of Absalom Cornet, a man sent from Scotland to root out alleged witchcraft. Cornet brings with him the threat of danger—and a pretty, young Norwegian wife named Ursa.

As Maren and Ursa are drawn to one another in ways that surprise them both, the island begins to close in on them, with Absalom's iron rule threatening Vardø's very existence.
catalogue.Author: Kiran-Millwood-Hargrave

Books.value: I Who Have Never Known Men
